extracted.intended_audience: educated readers of The Spectator; general literate public interested in literature, manners, education, and social criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Early-18th-century magazine essays offering prescriptive judgments and practical advice on literary composition (Milton's epic), child education, personal comportment (beauty, marriage), and social customs. The page mixes literary-critical standards with recommendations for education and manners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt speeches and actions to characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Circumstance in their Speeches and Actions is with great Justness and Delicacy adapted to the Persons who speak and act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author praises Milton for ensuring that characters' sentiments and behaviour conform to their characters (examples: Satan's mock-majesty and daring, Moloch's fury, Belial's timorousness, Mammon's covetousness). Use consistent characterization so that what a person says and does is believable given their established traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistency of character across contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Persons whom Milton introduces into his Poem always discover such Sentiments and Behaviour, as are in a peculiar manner conformable to their respective Characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character traits should persist across books/episodes (e.g., Belial is lewd and slothful in the first book and remains so later). Consistency provides unity and makes contrasts and debates effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align rhetorical role with rank/character
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prince of the fallen Angels opens and closes the Debate and is the proper Person to give great projects birth; others' speeches suit their dignity and station.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place speeches and proposals in the mouths of characters whose rank and temperament make them natural movers (e.g., Beelzebub as moderator and seconder of Satan's project). This preserves plausibility of council/debate scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contrast of thought for variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contrast of Thought in this Speech, and that which precedes it, gives an agreeable Variety to the Debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate differing viewpoints (rashness vs. sloth, fury vs. moderation) to enliven debates and avoid monotony. Contrasts should flow from character differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreshadow central project early
rubrics_metrics.description: It was just not to omit in the First Book the Project upon which the whole Poem turns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce the main motive or project of a long poem early so later developments feel grounded and organic (Milton alludes to the creation of Man early, which later becomes the poem's focus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy in descriptive episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: An ordinary Poet would have spun out so many Circumstances to a great Length, and by that means have weakned, instead of illustrated, the principal Fable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep episodes and descriptive passages concise and pregnant; avoid over-extending digressions that distract from the main narrative. A single striking line can be more effective than long-winded elaboration (example: a single line makes beasts of Hell more horrid than a long description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ concise, pregnant imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diversions of the fallen Angels... are described with great Pregnancy of Thought, and Copiousness of Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compact, vivid images (e.g., four Rivers disgorging into the Sea of Fire; monsters summarized in one line) to intensify reader imagination rather than dilute it with prolixity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match entertainments/actions to beings' nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diversions are every way suitable to Beings who had nothing left them but Strength and Knowledge misapplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting a society or group, make their amusements, music, and discourse reflect their established nature and history (e.g., fallen spirits celebrate criminal exploits; their music praises evil deeds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate allegory morally and artistically
rubrics_metrics.description: The Genealogy of the several Persons is contrived with great Delicacy... These are the Terrors of an evil Conscience, and the proper Fruits of Sin, which naturally rise from the Apprehensions of Death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegorical figures (Sin, Death) should be woven into the narrative so their symbolism reinforces the poem's moral point without breaking epic unity; their relations and actions should illustrate the intended moral meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt education to natural genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing but Nature can qualifie a Man for Learning... there should be certain Tryers or Examiners... to inspect the Genius of every particular Boy, and to allot him the Part that is most suitable to his natural Talents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess children's temperaments and aptitudes early and assign studies or trades that fit their natural capacities rather than forcing all into the same classical curriculum; examples cited: Marcus (Cicero's son) failed despite great opportunities; Clavius found aptitude in geometry after being marked hopeless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid one-size-fits-all schooling
rubrics_metrics.description: It is very usual to see forty or fifty Boys of several Ages, Tempers and Inclinations, ranged together in the same Class, employed upon the same Authors... they are all to be made Poets, Historians, and Orators alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not require identical tasks and authors for students of diverse abilities; tailor tasks, classes, and instruction to differences in genius, age, and inclination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public examination and assignment can serve the common good
rubrics_metrics.description: They might easily, by well examining the Parts of those under their Inspection, make a just Distribution of them into proper Classes and Divisions... allot to them this or that particular Study, as their Genius qualifies them for Professions, Trades, Handicrafts, or Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charity-schools or public institutions should test and sort pupils to maximise societal benefit, using early detection to direct talents into fitting professions (cites Spartan public discipline as example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-nature and cheerfulness outweigh mere beauty in lasting attraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Good-Nature will always supply the Absence of Beauty, but Beauty cannot long supply the Absence of Good-Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal qualities—cheerful, attentive, unselfish behaviour—make persons agreeable and secure affection more durably than physical beauty, which often accompanies impertinence and self-absorption; practical counsel includes cultivating easy behaviour and shedding vanity after loss of beauty (e.g., burn love-letters, adopt modesty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consciousness of unmerited approval breeds disappointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Endeavour to please is highly promoted by a Consciousness that the Approbation of the Person you would be agreeable to, is a Favour you do not deserve; for in this Case Assurance of Success is the most certain way to Disappointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humility and the awareness of being valued encourage efforts to please; over-assurance of success leads to complacency and later disappointment—apply this psychologically in comportment and social relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical officers to inspect consent in major social contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a Method founded upon Reason and Equity [to examine a wife's freedom in conveyance], why should there not be also a proper Officer for examining such as are entring into the State of Matrimony, whether they are forced by Parents... or moved by Interest only?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes institutional review of consent to marriage (analogous to judicial inquiry for conveyance) to prevent coerced matches and ensure marriages arise from free will rather than parental or financial pressure.
